title: Acceptance matrix for batching/cache cost tradeoffs
creator: Aisha Verma
description: Create a repeatable acceptance matrix and automated eval harness that ties batching and KV-cache recommendations to concrete quality gates and rollback rules. Must allow cost-saving config proposals to be applied automatically when they pass statistical non-inferiority tests across a stratified reference-prompt library and to fail safely with an automated rollback when gates are breached in canary/production.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance matrix defined: mapping of workload cohort -> metrics, thresholds, and test sizes (small/medium/large).
Automated eval harness implemented that runs proposed batching/cache configs against the current baseline and produces a human-review-ready report and pass/fail decision.
Canary rollout automation accepts config changes only when all cohort gates pass with pre-defined statistical confidence; otherwise it aborts and triggers rollback.
Rollback playbook documented and wired into the release job (GitHub Action) with clear alerting to oncall and PM.
Dashboard tile shows per-config expected cost delta, quality delta (per metric), and confidence interval; linkable from recommendation UI.

eval_suite_spec: Reference prompt library: 900 items partitioned into cohorts (short-chat, long-reason, code, summarization); each item has expected golden output and human-annotated acceptance label for 120 items sampled per cohort.

Primary metrics by cohort: embedding cosine similarity (openai/text-embedding-3-large) for natural language cohorts, BLEU/ROUGE-L for summarization, normalized edit distance and compilation correctness for code cohort, per-token logprob shift for worst-case hallucination signal.

Statistical test: paired bootstrap with 10k resamples to compute 95% CI on mean metric difference. Non-inferiority margins: embedding cosine >= -0.015 (absolute), human_accept_rate delta >= -1.5 percentage points, compilation-fail rate increase <= 0.5 percentage points.

Sample sizes: run full cohort for automated metrics; require at least 120 human-review samples across cohorts for human-accept_rate to consider promotion to production. Automated gate passes can short-circuit to canary but not to full rollout without human sample validation.

Signal aggregation: compute per-cohort p-values and a weighted company-wide quality score (weights: short-chat 0.25, long-reason 0.30, code 0.25, summarization 0.20) to reflect customer distribution estimated in usage telemetry.
apply_strategy: Dry-run in staging: run harness and store report; no config applied to traffic. Generate cost delta estimate and quality delta with CI.
Canary step: apply config to 1% of inference traffic in dedicated canary pool for 48 hours. Acceptance requires all automated gates pass and no user-visible errors (error rate <= baseline + 0.1%).
Shadow roll: If canary shows marginal pass (<80% power), run 24h shadow traffic capturing outputs for manual review but do not bill savings yet.

Progressive rollout: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% spaced by monitoring windows (2h, 6h, 24h, 48h) and requiring pass at each stage. All rollouts controlled by a single GitHub Action with parameters and guardrails.
rollback_playbook: Automated trigger conditions: automated gate failure in canary or production (metric breach beyond non-inferiority margin with 95% CI), error rate spike > baseline+1%, or manual abort from oncall/PM.

Immediate steps: revert config via runtime API to previous pinned model variant and config, disable batching changes, and route affected customers to fallback pool. GitHub Action will create a rollback PR and apply it automatically when automation triggers.
Notifications: page oncall, post summary to #infra-rollouts Slack channel, and create incident in Jira with prefilled template (links to harness run and failing metrics).
Post-rollback analysis: run the failing canary run under several alternates (smaller batch sizes, relaxed KV window) to isolate root cause; preserve all logs and traces for 30 days.
qa_notes: PM (Ravi) will coordinate a 1-day human review for the sampled human_accept_set once an automated pass occurs; aim for 120 human labels total sampled across cohorts.
Design to provide an example 'regression triage' UI mock for the ops dashboard (DES-Jordan-xxx).
SRE to add synthetic traffic scenario for long-sequence workloads during canary to exercise KV cache behavior.
estimated_savings: ~18% median token cost reduction for read-heavy chat workloads; projected ~$12k/month for pilot customers at current usage profiles
